question.problem: For the function $f(x,y,z)={e}^{4y-x{z}^{4}},$ evaluate $\frac{∂f}{∂x}$ at the point $(4,1,1).$
question.worked_solution:
We differentiate the given function with respect to $x,$ treating all other variables as constants. 

Using the chain rule, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({e}^{4y-x{z}^{4}}) \\  & ={e}^{4y-x{z}^{4}}\cdot \frac{∂}{∂x}(4y-x{z}^{4}).\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we use the sum and constant multiple rules:

$$
\begin{aligned}{e}^{4y-x{z}^{4}}\cdot \frac{∂}{∂x}(4y-x{z}^{4}) & ={e}^{4y-x{z}^{4}}\cdot (\frac{∂}{∂x}(4y)-\frac{∂}{∂x}(x{z}^{4})) \\  & ={e}^{4y-x{z}^{4}}\cdot (0-{z}^{4}\frac{∂}{∂x}(x)) \\  & ={e}^{4y-x{z}^{4}}\cdot (-{z}^{4})\cdot 1 \\  & =-{z}^{4}{e}^{4y-x{z}^{4}}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate the partial derivative at the point $(4,1,1):$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂z}{|}_{(4,1,1)} & =-(1)^{4}{e}^{4(1)-4(1)^{4}} \\  & =-1\end{aligned}
$$
